title: sdlc-supervisor completion report
description: Structured report an implementer returns for a task packet, replacing free-text 'here's what I did' summaries. If an implementer finds it needs to touch something outside its packet's read_paths/write_paths, it reports status 'scope_change_requested' rather than doing the out-of-scope work and mentioning it in a decisions note.

status.description: Outcome of this attempt. 'done': acceptance criteria met and (if the workflow calls for it) committed. 'scope_change_requested': the implementer determined it needs to read/write outside the packet's declared paths and stopped to ask rather than doing it -- a hard requirement of this framework's scope-contract model, not an implementer's judgment call to skip. 'blocked': cannot proceed for a reason outside the implementer's control (e.g. an unmet dependency, a missing credential/environment it isn't allowed to provision itself). 'failed': attempted the task and did not reach a done state (e.g. verification commands failed and further local attempts wouldn't help).

files_changed.description: Repo-relative paths actually created or modified this attempt. Should be a subset of the packet's write_paths; anything outside it is exactly what 'scope_change_requested' exists to flag instead of silently including here.

acceptance_results.description: One entry per criterion in the source packet's acceptance_criteria, in the same order, so a reader can line them up directly.

criterion.description: Copied verbatim from the packet's acceptance_criteria.

notes.description: Evidence or explanation; may be an empty string if met is true and self-evident, but should not be empty when met is false.

commands_run.description: One entry per verification (or other relevant) command actually executed.

summary.description: Short human-readable summary of the output (e.g. '387 tests, 0 failed'), not the raw log.

test_results.description: Free-form by design -- a project's test/verification shape varies enough by task (unit suite counts, manual throwaway-script verification with no runner, a live check under a supervisor role, etc.) that a single fixed structure would just get stringified into anyway. Typically a string summary, but any JSON value is accepted; the generator/consumers should not assume a specific shape here beyond 'present'.

decisions.description: Notable judgment calls made during the attempt, in scope, that a reviewer should know about.

scope_deviations.description: Anything that ended up differing from the packet's stated scope, even if minor and not rising to a full 'scope_change_requested' status (e.g. a read outside read_paths that turned out to be unavoidable and harmless). Distinct from status: scope_change_requested, which is for write-scope changes serious enough to halt and ask before proceeding.

unresolved_risks.description: Known gaps, caveats, or follow-ups the implementer is flagging rather than silently leaving implicit.

commit.description: Commit SHA once the work is committed on a feature branch, else null (e.g. status is blocked/failed/scope_change_requested, or the workflow leaves committing to the orchestrator).
